headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0058 — Your Microsoft 365 account changed while SMTO was using it

html:
SMTO-SKL-0058 — Your Microsoft 365 account changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: 72d55023-db00-5921-828f-ba336eedabf1
Slug: microsoft365-account-changed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The Microsoft 365 account SMTO was using was reconnected, edited or replaced partway through. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't act as the wrong account. An earlier step may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Outlook or OneDrive and check whether the email, meeting, contact or file change you asked for already happened. SMTO stopped partway, and repeating a step that already happened could send or change something twice.
  2. Ask anyone else who manages SMTO whether they just reconnected or edited the Microsoft 365 account, and wait until they are finished. Connecting or editing the account at the same time as a request causes this check to fail.
  3. Start a new message, type @ and pick the Microsoft 365 account again, then ask only for the parts that didn't happen. Picking the account again makes SMTO use its current, correct details.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the remaining work and its reply names the account you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't connect a different Microsoft account to get around this check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 account or OAuth app record changed between selection and use, failing the revision or identity check during token storage, disconnect or an operation.

What this means

  • Account/app revision fences or accepted identity checks detect changed saved profiles during token storage, disconnect or operation execution. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Account/app revision fences or accepted identity checks detect changed saved profiles during token storage, disconnect or operation execution.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare profile creation/revision and tenant/user/app identity, then inspect any prior provider receipts.

How to fix it

  • Reload the Microsoft 365 Account and its oauth_app_ref record in Parameter Store and confirm tenant_id, user_id and created_at are the intended identity; concurrent connect, disconnect or edits fail the revision fence. Check in Microsoft 365 whether any earlier mutation in the run already took effect, then re-select the current account (explicit account_ref or a fresh @ binding) before repeating only the work that did not happen.
  • Reload the exact account and OAuth app, reconcile prior effects, and deliberately select the current identity before remaining work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported recovery uses the intended current identity only after earlier effects are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
